cited_details.statement: As the KAIST-Radar (K-Radar) benchmark notes, "Radars use relatively longer wavelength radio bands (77∼81 GHz), resulting in robust measurements in adverse weathers," which motivates the development of learning-based perception pipelines tailored to radar's distinctive signal structure [https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2022/hash/185fdf627eaae2abab36205dcd19b817-Abstract-Datasets_and_Benchmarks.html].

The 2022 MDPI review "Towards Deep Radar Perception for Autonomous Driving" argues that "the era of deep learning for radar perception has arrived" and recommends three strategies to increase radar data density, namely "the use of pre-CFAR data, the use of high-resolution radar sensors, and the use of [learned processing]" [https://www.mdpi.com/1424-8220/22/11/4208].
The next generation of 4D radar can achieve imaging capability in the form of high-resolution point clouds" [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9185239/].

introduced **Deep Radar Detector**, a deep-learning pipeline that "work[s] directly with the radar complex data," bypassing handcrafted CFAR detectors and exploiting pre-detection information that classical pipelines discard [https://arxiv.org/pdf/1906.12187].
This pre-CFAR paradigm is explicitly endorsed by the MDPI review as a way to compensate for the sparsity of radar returns [https://www.mdpi.com/1424-8220/22/11/4208].
Three different 3D autoencoder based architectures are introduced to predict object confidence distribution from each snippet of the input RAMaps" [https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.01816].

The 2020 IJCNN paper "Range-Doppler Detection in Automotive Radar with Deep Learning" presents "a comprehensive study on radar detection using deep learning with application to automotive vehicles," treating the RDM as the primary tensor for classifier design [http://vigir.ee.missouri.edu/~gdesouza/Research/Conference_CDs/IEEE_WCCI_2020/IJCNN/Papers/N-21054.pdf].

The follow-up CRUW3D release (introduced in the RODNet lineage) "includes 66K synchronized and well-calibrated camera, radar, and LiDAR frames in various driving scenarios," demonstrating the maturation of RAMap-style benchmarks and the value of cross-modal labels even when training radar-only networks [https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/RODNet%3A-Radar-Object-Detection-using-Cross-Modal-Wang-Jiang/3b858058c04da3871848b81e8d8304e24c1282d5].

Conventional 3D radar tensors (3DRT) contain power along Doppler, range, and azimuth but lack elevation, "so it is challenging to estimate the 3D bounding box of an object from 3DRT" [https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2022/hash/185fdf627eaae2abab36205dcd19b817-Abstract-Datasets_and_Benchmarks.html].

The K-Radar benchmark (NeurIPS 2022) addresses this by introducing a **4D Radar Tensor (4DRT)** that "contain[s] power measurements along the Doppler, range, azimuth, and elevation dimensions, together with carefully annotated 3D bounding box labels." The dataset provides 35K frames "in challenging driving conditions such as adverse weathers (fog, rain, and snow) on various road structures (urban, suburban roads, alleyways, and highways)" [https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2022/hash/185fdf627eaae2abab36205dcd19b817-Abstract-Datasets_and_Benchmarks.html].

The MDPI survey frames this shift as a transition toward "imaging capability in the form of high-resolution point clouds," where "the era of deep learning for radar perception has arrived" and "studies on radar deep learning are spread across different tasks" [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9185239/].

The 2024 paper "Camera–Radar Fusion with Modality Interaction and Radar Gaussian [Splatting]" argues that "the fusion of millimeter-wave radar and camera modalities is crucial for improving the accuracy and completeness of 3-dimensional (3D) object [detection]" and proposes to lift sparse radar returns into continuous Gaussian primitives, which can be splatted onto the image plane for attention-based fusion [https://spj.science.org/doi/pdf/10.34133/cbsystems.0079].

While not the focus of a single primary source here, the MDPI survey highlights grid-based encodings as one of the canonical outputs of the radar signal processing chain [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9185239/].

This can benefit from using off-the-shelf single sensor detection algorithms, but late fusion cannot fully exploit the complementary properties of sensors" [https://underline.io/lecture/69109-craft-camera-radar-3d-object-detection-with-spatio-contextual-fusion-transformer].

To overcome this, CRAFT introduces a **proposal-level early fusion** that "associates image proposal with radar points in the polar coordinate system to efficiently handle the discrepancy between the coordinate system and spatial properties," then applies cross-attention layers to exchange spatio-contextual features [https://underline.io/lecture/69109-craft-camera-radar-3d-object-detection-with-spatio-contextual-fusion-transformer].

The reported gains—41.1% mAP and 52.3% NDS on the nuScenes test set, "8.7 and 10.8 points higher than the camera-only baseline"—illustrate how representation-aware fusion exploits the polar geometry that is intrinsic to radar [https://underline.io/lecture/69109-craft-camera-radar-3d-object-detection-with-spatio-contextual-fusion-transformer].

The MDPI review categorizes micro-Doppler as one of the principal radar representations and discusses its role in scene understanding beyond bounding-box detection [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9185239/].

CRUW introduced synchronized camera–radar RAMap data with cross-modal labels [https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.01816], CRUW3D extended this to "66K synchronized and well-calibrated camera, radar, and LiDAR frames" [https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/RODNet%3A-Radar-Object-Detection-using-Cross-Modal-Wang-Jiang/3b858058c04da3871848b81e8d8304e24c1282d5], and K-Radar added elevation and adverse-weather coverage via the 4DRT [https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2022/hash/185fdf627eaae2abab36205dcd19b817-Abstract-Datasets_and_Benchmarks.html].

Second, **geometric fidelity**: 3DRT lacks elevation, which motivates 4DRT and Gaussian primitives [https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2022/hash/185fdf627eaae2abab36205dcd19b817-Abstract-Datasets_and_Benchmarks.html, https://spj.science.org/doi/pdf/10.34133/cbsystems.0079].

Third, **cross-modal alignment**: polar coordinate systems and Doppler axes make naïve feature concatenation with cameras suboptimal, motivating representation-aware fusion designs such as CRAFT [https://underline.io/lecture/69109-craft-camera-radar-3d-object-detection-with-spatio-contextual-fusion-transformer].

The 2022 MDPI survey's prescription—"use of pre-CFAR data, the use of high-resolution radar sensors, and the use of [learned processing]"—remains the most concise statement of the field's near-term trajectory [https://www.mdpi.com/1424-8220/22/11/4208].
